hints: Focus on what LiAlH4 does, it turns each C=O of an aldehyde or ketone into a CH-OH group without changing the carbon skeleton.
Draw out 4-methylpentane-2,3-diol as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH(CH}_3)_2$ and notice the two OH groups are on adjacent carbons 2 and 3.
Work backwards by changing both CH-OH groups back to C=O and check which option has two carbonyls in exactly those 2 and 3 positions on the same skeleton.
walkthrough:
**Recall LiAlH4 reduction**

LiAlH4 is a strong reducing agent. It reduces aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols.

$$\text{R-CHO} \rightarrow \text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}, \quad \text{R-CO-R'} \rightarrow \text{R-CH(OH)-R'}$$

**Draw the product skeleton**

The product is 4-methylpentane-2,3-diol. Its carbon backbone is unchanged by reduction.

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$$
This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH(CH}_3)_2$, with OH on C2 and C3.

**Reverse the reduction to find R**

To get an OH on C2 and an OH on C3, R must have had a C=O on C2 and a C=O on C3. So R must be 4-methylpentane-2,3-dione.

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CO}-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$$

**Match to the options**

Only the structure with $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-$ next to $-\text{CO}-\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$ has ketones at C2 and C3 on the correct branched chain. That is the correct identity for R.

options.A: This is 4-methylpentane-2,3-dione, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCOCH(CH}_3)_2$. Reduction of both ketone C=O groups with LiAlH4 gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH(CH}_3)_2$, which is exactly 4-methylpentane-2,3-diol.
options.B: This is an aldehyde-ketone with C=O at C1 and C2, $\text{OHC-CO-CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$. Reduction would give a 1,2-diol, $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$, not a 2,3-diol.
options.C: This is 3-methylpentane-2,4-dione, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3)\text{COCH}_3$. The carbonyls are separated at C2 and C4, so reduction would give 3-methylpentane-2,4-diol, not the 2,3-diol.
options.D: This is 2-methyl-3-oxopentanal, $\text{OHC-CH(CH}_3)\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The carbonyls are at C1 and C3, so reduction would give a 1,3-diol, not the required adjacent 2,3-diol.
